rationale: Round 0 built and passed, so headroom exists to raise obfuscation on this 37-function, 2.3 KB C++ program whose hot spots are the Array/SpArray constructor-destructor pairs. SUB is weighted highest: arithmetic substitution is cheap in both size and time and this code is constructor-driven with plenty of integer index/size math to transform. FLA stays strong since the largest functions (Array ctor 217 B, Insert 208 B) are control-flow-rich enough to flatten profitably, but its RuntimeCost weight is moderate because Insert is on the program's hot path. BCF is kept mid-range with elevated SizeCost because bogus edges inflate a tiny 2.3 KB text segment quickly; modest application still adds decoy paths without doubling the binary. SPLIT gets high DiversityGain and near-zero costs as the safest way to break up the duplicated C1/C2 and D1/D2 bodies, hindering clone-based pattern matching. IBR is moderate — useful displacement on basic-block boundaries but with real per-block dispatch cost. ICALL keeps a decent DiversityGain to convert direct calls (e.g., Insert->Array helpers) into indirect ones, tempered by the highest CorrectnessRisk of the set given vtable-heavy C++ code where indirect-call rewriting must not touch virtual dispatch. IGV is included lightly for global/constant concealment with low costs but a caution flag, since over-encoding globals in a tiny benchmark risks init-order issues.
